answer: Agents can require each identity to lock a scarce token in a vault before it may vote or claim rewards, then slash that stake if independent audits find duplicate-controlled accounts. A Sybil operator must therefore buy and immobilize capital for every fake identity; multiplying accounts no longer creates influence for free. The rising cost can spiral as the attacker scales, while a sudden plume of newly funded identities becomes a visible signal for review—not proof of fraud on its own.
